title: Full AWS enterprise deployment architecture

nodes.title: Authenticated intake
nodes.note: JWT identity + custom business approval checks
nodes.study: Regional API stage uses WAF and Cognito authorisation. Intake Lambda independently validates tenant, stakeholder scope and exact contract revision. Separate worker ingress uses IAM/SigV4; it never trusts human JWT claims as state authority.

nodes.title: Planning
nodes.note: Propose owned DAG; Core admits exact revision

nodes.title: Authoritative run ledger
nodes.study: Partition by tenant/run; conditional revisions and transactions guard approval, owner acceptance, task attempts, reservations and release intent. Use current/strongly consistent reads where decisions need them; atomically recheck at commit. S3, DynamoDB and external systems share no distributed transaction. Commit ledger + outbox after exact artifact verification; reconcile delivery.

nodes.title: Exact artifacts & evidence
nodes.study: Separate candidate, assurance, immutable pattern and released-package namespaces. Builder writes candidates; independent verifier reads exact candidates and writes evidence; release can publish only admitted versions. KMS key and bucket policies explicitly grant cross-account access. Optional Object Lock applies retention to exact object versions; it cannot validate correctness.

nodes.title: Validated completion broker
nodes.study: Cross-account jobs submit signed completion envelopes carrying run/task/attempt/epoch and object versions/digests to a narrow Control API. The broker verifies the admitted attempt and current authority, records validated completion/provenance idempotently, and only then uses a protected task token. Step Functions callback tokens require a principal in the same account as the state machine. Token arrival is transport completion, never owner acceptance; Core still requires the independent owner, test, PIC and final predicates.

nodes.title: Restore
nodes.note: Revalidate pins, digests and current authority

nodes.title: Candidate
nodes.note: Proposal only; cannot alter running version

nodes.title: Bounded Repair
nodes.note: Bounded repair; never retry unknown effects

nodes.title: Observability
nodes.note: OTEL traces, metrics and capacity evidence

nodes.title: Capability Gap
nodes.note: Affected work blocks until qualified binding

nodes.title: Permission Boundary
nodes.note: Effect scope, fence and budget admission

nodes.title: Approved target credentials
nodes.note: Scoped credentials; never distributed to builders
nodes.study: The governed adapter obtains only a reviewed target credential. Identity authenticates the caller and manages supported credentials; custom AC checks decide permitted resource, purpose, budget and attempt. Gateway Policy must use ENFORCE. Receiver-side idempotency/fencing or reconciliation is still required for external effects.

nodes.title: Account-wide service identities
nodes.note: Account policy facet; planner ≠ builder ≠ verifier ≠ releaser
nodes.study: IAM is an account-wide/global control facet shown beside regional enforcement, not a service hosted in a subnet or Region. Dedicated roles and trust policies scope each service. Core may assume only qualified dispatch roles; build cannot write authority state or assurance evidence; assurance cannot mutate candidate artifacts. Cross-account access needs both identity/trust and resource/KMS policy review. SCPs and permissions boundaries restrict maximum grants; they do not grant access. Review real IAM evaluation including resource policies and explicit denies.

nodes.title: Approved model access
nodes.study: Runtime hosts qualified reasoning code; Bedrock provides inference. Contract, plan, candidate and domain roles can invoke only approved models under data classification and Region constraints. Guardrails filters selected content risks; it is not PIC, IAM, domain correctness or release authority. Runtime session data is not the trusted run ledger. A custom adapter handles exact output artifacts; bounded jobs may alternatively use the optimized Step Functions InvokeHarness integration subject to its 15-minute/text-only/no-stop limitations.

nodes.title: Encryption & attestation keys
nodes.note: SSE-KMS for objects; SIGN_VERIFY for attestations
nodes.study: Separate encryption keys from asymmetric SIGN_VERIFY attestation keys. Scope key policies and grants by producer/consumer account. TLS protects service transport. Sign exact release manifests; a signature establishes provenance/integrity under key custody, not the business correctness of its content.

nodes.title: Execution
nodes.note: Admitted work; separate bounded job tasks

nodes.title: AZ-independent scheduling
nodes.note: Each job role can run in either eligible subnet
nodes.study: Positions show example placement, not fixed role-to-AZ affinity. ECS RunTask placement accepts qualified subnets in both AZs. Independent finite task definitions implement executor, integrator and specialist construction. Bounded deadlines, per-job roles, no broad egress and ECR digest pins are required. Fargate isolation is not a claim that arbitrary hostile generated code is safely sandboxed.

nodes.title: Private service endpoint paths
nodes.service: S3 gateway; ECR API/DKR, logs and Control API interfaces
nodes.note: Endpoint and resource policies narrow access
nodes.study: S3 gateway endpoint policy scopes admitted object access. ECR API and Docker registry interface endpoints plus S3 layers enable qualified image pull; CloudWatch Logs uses its supported interface endpoint. Use a private IAM-authenticated Control API with an execute-api endpoint where appropriate. Confirm service/Region support, private DNS, TLS and security-group ingress for each required endpoint. No public NAT route is implied.

nodes.title: Qualified build images
nodes.note: Pipeline tests images before registry admission
nodes.study: ECR stores reviewed container images. Pipeline validation binds scan/test evidence to a digest, task definition and capability schema. Workers cannot promote their own images. Private image pull needs the supported ECR endpoints and S3 layer access; logs need their own endpoint path.

nodes.title: Verification
nodes.note: Independent exact evidence; Core commits acceptance

nodes.title: Final Validation
nodes.note: Exact final test attestation; managed helper outside VPC

nodes.title: Independent endpoint policies
nodes.service: S3 gateway; ECR API/DKR, logs and Control API interfaces
nodes.note: Candidate read-only; assurance prefix write only
nodes.study: Assurance uses separate endpoint security groups and policies. It reads only exact admitted candidate inputs and writes its own evidence namespace. Cross-account S3/KMS grants are explicit. Private callback ingress returns through the narrow Control API; neither evidence upload nor a valid task token confers owner acceptance.

nodes.title: Accountable owner decision ingress
nodes.note: I066 decision is independent of worker result
nodes.study: One accountable owner per work unit independently attests acceptance through the Control account API hosted in Control. Evidence generation and owner acceptance are separate. Verification completion does not imply acceptance. Core checks owner identity, approved test obligations, exact artifact digest and current dependencies before recording AcceptedCurrent.

nodes.title: Managed verification / final helpers
nodes.note: Managed service outside VPC; Core independently gates acceptance
nodes.study: Lambda validates structured verifier/final results and PIC evidence outside customer VPCs, then submits exact digest-bound attestation manifests to the Control broker. Lambda runs in AWS-managed infrastructure; a customer VPC attachment creates networking ENIs, not an in-subnet function host. Fargate subnet cards represent test runners only. Helpers cannot write current acceptance/release state; Core separately checks independent owner, tests, dependencies, PIC and current approval.

nodes.title: Qualified independent tests
nodes.note: Read exact candidates; write assurance prefix only
nodes.study: Verifier, final validation, assurance specialist and controlled-learning evaluation use separate task definitions and evidence namespaces; they may be scheduled in either eligible AZ subnet. They cannot alter candidates, business approval, release records or active configuration pins. Security independence depends on actual policies, test trust and administrator separation, not account boxes alone.

nodes.title: Contract-selected runtime
nodes.note: Single or multiple workers; inherited owner/guard/test controls
nodes.study: The released WorkflowSpec declares the required runtime, dependencies, roles, accepted image/model/pattern pins and evidence controls. A separately authorised target deployment role validates the package and installs its controls. Deployment cannot inherit unlimited engineering-system authority. The generated workflow must enforce its own equivalent pattern guard/test/evidence bindings.

nodes.title: Governed target adapters
nodes.study: This box is the target-owned adapter boundary, not the external SaaS/on-prem system. External enterprise APIs and domain data remain separate trust boundaries outside the AWS organization. Target execution calls only approved adapters under target authority. Reconcile uncertain effects; no blind non-idempotent retry. Data access, residency and postconditions depend on the selected business use case and cannot be inferred from the reference diagram.

nodes.title: External enterprise systems
nodes.note: Independent target identity, data and effect boundary
nodes.study: These systems are outside the AWS enterprise organization. Only approved engineering or workflow adapters may invoke allowed resources under separately granted target credentials. The domain contract defines idempotency, reconciliation, data residency and observable success. Timeout is not proof that an effect failed.

nodes.title: Central security audit
nodes.note: Selected management/data events; separate from acceptance
nodes.study: Organization trail and selected data events record relevant API activity into a separate protected archive. CloudWatch/AgentCore operational traces use correlation IDs with sensitive content redaction and retention. Neither log stream automatically supplies domain test acceptance. Baseline audit/metrics exist even when optional Recovery is off; observe adds recovery/capacity analysis.

nodes.title: Operations & incident response
nodes.note: Trace run/task/attempt; alarm on blockers and failed release
nodes.study: Monitor admission latency, pending approvals, model/tool latency, throttles, candidate rejection, uncertain effects, expired attempts, DLQ age and release receipt lag. Define alarm owners, incident runbooks and measured SLOs per use case. Collect only approved model/tool trace content; segregate audit, operational telemetry and exact acceptance evidence.

nodes.title: Platform lifecycle / IaC
nodes.service: Reviewed IaC · CI/CD · dev → preprod → prod
nodes.note: Approved artifacts, policies and conformance tests
nodes.study: Deploy isolated copies of this topology per environment. Version state-machine definitions, Lambda code, task definitions, image digests, policy and pattern manifests. Run negative/fault tests and smoke tests in preproduction before authorised production promotion. Platform deployment is distinct from releasing a generated MOA Workflow. Choose the organization’s established pipeline; avoid an unnecessary parallel tooling stack.

nodes.title: Availability & recovery admission
nodes.note: One authoritative Region; no invented RTO/RPO
nodes.study: Select the authoritative Region from service/model availability, residency and enterprise policy. Measure throughput and per-service concurrency against quotas. AZ placement and managed service durability do not establish an end-to-end SLO. A regional outage stops new authority decisions; documented backup/restore requires reconciliation, current pins and operator approval. Propose a second Region only after RTO/RPO and recovery consistency are justified.
